page.layout: One page of text in the centre; below it a large woodcut of a flower basket and the word FINIS above it; show-through from the reverse side in the background (not transcribed).

main_text.p: Respice non torvo Parnasia munera vultu, Gratulor ex animo Carmine namque tibi: Omnia sic cedant feliciter omine laeto, Robore teque suo roboret Omnipotens Deiicias hostes, doctrinae pondere sternas, Ut nobis vivas laetus honore tuo: O! per te nomen magnum, sic gloria surget Nomen in orbe tuum semper erit celebre, Laudes ipse tuas extendam ego ad astra polumque: Exclamabo: Omnes nunc celebrate meum Pectore, quem socium longo cognoscitis usu, Res bene succedat: Carmina laetum ego, Haecce Georg Hollard scripsi Sophiae Studiosus, Us u quem poteris semper habere tuum.
main_text.head: FINIS.
main_text.p: [woodcut of a flower basket, not transcribed]

page.notes: The first letters of the opening lines are large decorated initials (R, O, D, U, O, L, E, P, R, H, U) and have been read as printed; the initial of line "Haecce" and "Us" are partly damaged. Lines of the verse are set as printed; the first line of the verse block is "Respice non torvo Parnasia munera vultu," with the initial R. The Latin line "Deiicias" is printed with a damaged "D" and may read "Dejicias". Show-through of the reverse page (printer's imprint, with "Typis Andreae Hogenbergii" in mirror text) is not transcribed.
